newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OSCE says Albania Socialists won about 60 pct.
newsitem.headline: OSCE says Albania Socialists won about 60 pct.

text.p: A top OSCE election observer said on Wednesday that Albania's Socialists probably got about 60 percent of the vote in last Sunday's poll and that voter turnout was in the region of 70 percent.
Catherine Lalumiere, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe's special Albania coordinator, said that only about 55 percent of returns were in but that the result was obvious.
"The direction is clear. It is the Socialists who have won," Lalumiere, a French Euro-MP, told a news conference.
Both Albanian Socialist party leader Fatos Nano and his opponent, President Sali Berisha, have said that the Socialists won.
Lalumiere repeated the OSCE's findings that there that been irregularities but that the election had been adequate to get the seal of approval from the Western observers.
"Albania is not a country like others," she said. "(But) at the end of the day we were satisfied enough."
Some of the irregularities, she said, could simply be put down to Albanians lack of experience as voters.
"Albanians don't know how to vote (privately)," she said. "They vote as a family. But it is hardly a crime."
